architect.reply:
Yes
The design is sound, minimal, and cleanly enforceable. Recording the seat, stop action, and timestamp directly in the card's rulings provides an auditable trail without needing new tooling or file formats. Stopping background processes explicitly by task or process ID prevents false positives and accidental termination of unrelated tasks. Enforcing foreground waits for lock contention removes orphan watchers at the architectural root. Bounding the rule as a three-card trial with explicit metrics (two-driver events target zero, counter-metric on idle minutes) ensures the process change is empirically evaluated before permanent adoption.
CITE: records in the card's rulings the seat, the stop and the time
